lead.description: the probability beyond a cutoff, or the direction in which a histogram decays slowly

self_checks.title: An SAT cutoff
self_checks.prompt: SAT scores follow a normal model with mean 1100 and standard deviation 200. What is the upper-tail probability at 1190?
self_checks.answer: The standardised value is 0.45 and the upper tail is 0.3264.

self_checks.title: A standard point
self_checks.prompt: The standard normal lower tail at z = 1 is 0.8413447. What is the upper tail?

self_checks.title: An exponential cutoff
self_checks.prompt: For a unit exponential, what is the upper-tail probability at 2, to six decimals?

overview_sentence: A [tail](articles/tail.qmd) is the probability beyond a cutoff, or the slow decay of a histogram in one direction.
